Physics of the driver: site/data/knowledge_topics.json, fabric topic "How it works": "A home's space-heating demand is, to a good approximation, its heat-loss coefficient ... multiplied by how cold it has been over the season, less the heat the sun and the occupants supply for free"; docs/market_research/gas_demand_what_drives_it_and_the_term_the_model_is_missing.md "Controls and end-use split": "Domestic gas end use is roughly 75% space heating (DESNZ 2024), with hot water 12-25% and cooking 5-10%"; docs/market_research/gas_demand_cumulative_hdd_cwv.md, National Grid Gas Demand Forecasting Methodology 2020: "Effective temperature takes into account the previous day's temperature due to consumer behaviour" (demand is regressed on weather). Year-to-year variation in the driver: docs/market_research/other_market_germany_2026-10-25.md (and other_market_japan): "UK HDD 2,710-2,961 over 2018-2025 (2024: 2,812)" (Eurostat nrg_chdd_a) - an annual spread of about 9%, and a single month averages fewer days than a year so its HDD varies at least as much (strong logic); docs/market_research/how_a_supplier_shapes_an_estimate_for_an_unread_month.md section 4: "January 2025 ran markedly colder than January 2023-2024, visible in the per-year shares", and January carries "17.05%" of domestic gas against July "2.33%" (DESNZ Energy Trends 4.2). Weather plus price in the record: docs/market_research/how_much_a_same_households_use_moves_year_on_year_and_in_2022.md section 2B, DESNZ ECUK Table C9, domestic gas 2021 to 2022 "-11.6%" temperature-corrected and "-19.2%" unadjusted (weather alone about 7.6 points of annual use in one year); section 2A SERL: gas "10.8% lower than the previous winter (accounting for weather)", IQR "(1.19%, 22.44%)"; section 1: "some households continued to use up to around 1 kWh of electricity per day or 15-20% more than predicted throughout 2021/22, others decreased by similar levels" (individual households swing by much more than the sample median). Why a repeat signals a shape, not a meter: how_a_supplier_shapes_an_estimate_for_an_unread_month.md section 3, Xoserve: AQ is "An estimate of the amount of gas (in kWh) that a supply meter point will use in the coming year under 'seasonal normal' weather conditions", spread monthly by the Annual Load Profile; a fixed AQ times a fixed seasonal-normal profile repeats month for month. Reasoning for the bounds (belief): on a ~1,400 kWh January, weather alone (annual ~5-9%, monthly more) and behaviour put the same-month year-on-year difference at a spread of tens of kWh; the chance that a difference with that spread lands inside a 0.1 kWh window is of order 0.1/50, about 0.2% per winter pair; summer months (~2-3% of annual use, smaller spread) perhaps nearer 1%. A leg of 2016-2025 has at most ~108 pairs, so the expected count is below 1, and 3 or more (or a winter run across 2022) is not credible. Leg B: weather alone moved national annual gas ~7.6 points in 2021-22 and individual households swing 15-20%, so a median winter year-on-year change below 1% across a leg is not a weather-driven home; the 1% floor is the lenient end of a 1-3% belief range (F11, erring against the thesis that the record is defective).

On the 85b044be54 pages the seat counts 1,635 of 4,413 gas month-pairs read A or M at both ends repeating to 0.1 kWh, 114 of 383 legs repeating on 10% or more of their pairs. GAP (1): no file read gives monthly GB heating-degree-day series or their year-to-year spread by calendar month; the Eurostat figure is annual UK (2,710-2,961, 2018-2025), and the monthly spread is inferred as at least the annual one (strong logic, not a number read). The 0.2%/1% per-pair coincidence figures, the R_g thresholds 1/2/3, the book share 1%, and the dispersion floor f (1-3%) are stated beliefs with the reasoning above, not sourced constants. GAP (2): no GB study publishes a same-household, weather-corrected, ordinary-year distribution of year-on-year change (how_much_a_same_households_use_moves_year_on_year_and_in_2022.md section 1, "That is a GAP"); individual-household monthly spread is therefore bounded from the SERL 15-20% remark and the 2022/23 IQR, not measured. GAP (3): whether a supplier's record holds a CALENDAR-month kWh on actual reads at all depends on read frequency: a quarterly- or annually-read credit meter has no actual read at month ends, so its monthly kWh is apportioned; the row excludes apportioned months, and if the record cannot distinguish apportioned from read-bounded months the row is ungradable for that leg (reported as such, not passed). Smart gas meters (daily/monthly reads) and prepayment meters are where read-bounded calendar months exist; no file read establishes the read frequency of either in 2016-2025. GAP (4): prepayment gas months are included as measured per the brief, but no file read establishes how a prepayment record's monthly kWh is formed (meter vend/credit data versus reads); if it is derived from vends or an AQ, leg A grades the derivation, not the meter. GAP (5): an AQ-driven ESTIMATE that repeats last year is lawful and expected (Xoserve seasonal-normal AQ); the defect graded here is a repeat carried on months labelled actual, and the row cannot by itself tell a mislabelled estimate from a mis-sourced measured value.
